reviewer_type: Three AI reviewers inspecting actual images; no separate human signoff claimed

scope.personal_and_delegated_inspection: Coordinator personally inspected22 Guardian/UI sheets; receipt_binding independently inspected18 common-death sheets; hexer_visual independently inspected16 Hexer phrase sheets. The coordinator verifies and preserves their signed reviewer identities and leaf receipts; does not claim to have personally re-viewed delegated sheets.
scope.image_origin: Lossy H264-decoded frames plus JPEG92 4:4:4 contact sheets, original1:1 composition pixels with labels; every actual viewer requested original detail. No native Godot PNG or whole-movie viewing claim.

conclusions: Both static ending UI pairs are readable and show the same victory/reward summary,2 RELICS and first VEILGLASS CONDUCTOR name; second item card is outside the shown viewport.

Raiders retain comparable backward falls. AFTER Hexer,Bulwark,Elite and Guardian show clearer human silhouettes; Elite and Guardian backward collapse is particularly readable. Dark floor/hero/staff overlap limit Hexer/Bulwark death detail.

Guardian phase1/2 timing and annulus/lane then split-ring/lane warnings are legible; AFTER has broad torso/arm/bell sweeps and an upright return by2206-2217. Late body-release poses vary less than floor/HUD impact cues.

Hexer warning/impact timings visually match, first recovery is lethally interrupted and additional recovery survives through reset831. AFTER Hexer body/staff release and recovery cues are weak relative to the baseline raised-staff sweep; ground rings carry timing.
No blanket polished-animation acceptance is given. These records complete only the explicitly sampled context inspection with quality concerns and limits preserved.
limits: Only retained contact-sheet panels were actually viewed, not all2496 frames of either movie.
Each first-death range covers the initial0.97s after lethal event; complete skeletal death and long-term settling are not approved.
Raider/Hexer first-death sheets duplicate the same simultaneous frame9-39 window; they are shared temporal evidence, despite every requested file being actually viewed.
No phase0 Guardian warning/impact occurs; Guardian is actor50 for region0 and internal phases1/2 correspond to HUD phases2/3.
No native ankle/shin positions, anatomical metrics, unviewed rendered-pixel occlusion, physical phone FPS, universal correctness or human signoff inferred.
Image compression, dark lighting, overlapping silhouettes and sampled time gaps constrain fine-detail motion judgments.

viewed_files.label: first-boss-death
observations: BEFORE f2259 shows the tall ribbed bell/cylindrical Guardian silhouette. Lethal f2261 removes boss HUD and foe count becomes0. Later retained frames show the bell body leaning and falling left until a horizontal dark body/bell silhouette remains by f2279-2289.

AFTER f2259-2263 shows an articulated bareheaded humanoid with shoulder armor and a large pale bell-headed weapon. During f2267-2275 knees/torso lower and the body rolls backward with the weapon moving from raised to lowered. Byf2279-2289 head/torso are rightward and legs/weapon leftward in a readable horizontal body silhouette.

Both pairs keep the hero, reliquary and chamber framing readable as UI changes to Recover the reliquary. No obvious large corpse teleport, disappearance below floor or detached limb is apparent in these retained game-scale panels. This is the first 0.97 seconds of the death response, not proof of complete skeletal death/settling.

viewed_files.label: first-boss-telegraph-release-recovery-reset
observations: Paired f2094 displays HUD PHASE1 CROWNED VIGIL, f2096 changes to PHASE2 CROWN BREAK, and f2153 changes to PHASE3 FINAL TOLL. These correspond to journal internal phases 0, 1, 2; actual boss actor identity50 is supplied by the journal, not inferred solely from pixels.

Internal phase 1 warning at f2099 is a clear orange annulus with diagonal cleaving lane. Countdown remains legible through f2143. Atf2144 the warning becomes a solid pale orange impact footprint. Ring center/lane shape and before-after timing visually line up.

AFTER has a readable human torso, bending knees and broad free-arm/bell-weapon sweeps through f2099-2126. Compared with the baseline bell cylinder this makes whole-body action more distinct. The later low body/bell pose changes little across retained f2130-2144; exact impact timing reads most strongly from the floor fill and HUD change, rather than a large immediate body silhouette change.

Internal phase 2 warning at f2156 uses two overlapping orange ring footprints and a diagonal lane, followed by a broad human arm/weapon sweep in AFTER f2158-2178. A low body/bell pose is again retained nearf2185-2196. Ground footprint turns solid at f2198, hero life changes 380 to 357 and WARD 12 label appears; paired floor/HUD timing matches.

After the second impact the AFTER Guardian rises more upright by f2206-2210; the warning/impact footprint is absent at f2213 and actual native reset boundary f2213-2214 is retained. Guardian stands beside the hero in laterf2217. No large pose pop or conspicuous new detached part is apparent in the retained panels.

Hero and Guardian overlap around both late warning/impact moments, and small compressed silhouettes limit precise grip, foot contact and body-release assessment. Every retained sheet was inspected, not every consecutive decoded frame. No phase 0 Guardian warning/impact occurs in the underlying recorded sequence.
